court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: K.Muruganandam vs State Rep. By on 1 February, 2022

parties.respondent_defendant: State rep. By / The Deputy Superintendent of Police, Rasipuram, Rasipuram Police Station

facts_of_case: Appellants were arrayed as Accused Nos.1, 3 to 6 and 8 to 10 before the trial Court. A1 married PW.1/Dhamayanthi on 05.04.2001. Out of their wedlock a male child was born to the de facto complainant on 29.01.2002.

legal_principles.principle: The police have no power to register a case under Sec.494 IPC and this type of complaints ought to have been given only as per Section 198 Cr.P.C.
legal_principles.held: This court holds that the police have no power to investigate such kind of offences; since PW.1 misbehaved with A1, he moved away from her and established his practice at Ariyalur;

legal_principles.principle: Only an Officer not below the rank of DSP alone can investigate the offences falling under the Act;
legal_principles.held: As per Sec.14 of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,1989 only an Officer not below the rank of DSP alone can investigate such kind of offences;
applicable_acts_sections: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act — Sec.14

outcome.result: Appeal filed under Section 378 Cr.P.C., against the judgement of sentences and fine imposed in S.C.No.196/2003
outcome.final_order: This Criminal Appeal has been filed by the appellants/accused to set aside the judgement of conviction imposed in S.C.No.196/2003.
